baseline.note: Library citations read at the pinned commit: Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean (HenselianRing R I with fields jac and is_henselian for monic polynomials; HenselianLocalRing with TFAE; IsAdicComplete.henselianRing). The pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no spectra-level algebraic K-theory, THH/TC, cyclotomic spectra, de Rham–Witt complexes, henselization of pairs or nonunital henselian rings (declaration index searched for Henselization, Cyclotomic, TopologicalHochschild, DeRhamWitt, AlgebraicKTheory, Nonunital).

summary: Clausen, Mathew and Morrow prove that for a henselian pair (R, I) the relative K-theory and relative topological cyclic homology agree with finite coefficients: K^inv(R) → K^inv(R/I) is an equivalence mod p (Theorem A). This extends Gabber rigidity (n invertible) and the profinite Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem (I nilpotent). The key new input is that TC/p commutes with all colimits on connective cyclotomic spectra (Theorem G), proved by showing that the Frobenius of HF_p^triv kills the periodicity class. That finiteness enters a pseudocoherence formalism for functors on henselian nonunital rings, which axiomatizes the first half of Gabber's proof. The equal-characteristic case comes from Geisser–Levine and Geisser–Hesselholt. Consequences: K/p and TC/p agree in high degrees for rings henselian along p with finite p-rank residue fields (Theorem B, a p-adic Lichtenbaum–Quillen statement); K^inv/p vanishes at strictly henselian points (Theorem C) and p-adic étale K-theory of schemes proper over such rings is TC; the trace is split injective for local F_p-algebras (Theorem D); K-theory is continuous for F-finite complete noetherian rings (Theorem F), and not without F-finiteness (Theorem 5.7); p-adic continuity of K for rings henselian along p; and a pro Geisser–Levine theorem (Theorem E). The atlas plans cyclotomic spectra, the trace and Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy (RefinedTraceMethods RT.2–RT.3), Gabber rigidity away from p (KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.2), K-theory foundations and de Rham–Witt theory. The paper's own theory goes to a new Part II of RefinedTraceMethods, p-adic continuity to the AMMN Part II, Gabber's affine proper base change to ArcTopologyAndDescent, and standard inputs to sources of existing layers. Seven misprints are recorded; no error or gap was found.

items.name: The fibre of the cyclotomic trace K^inv
items.statement: For a ring R (more generally a connective E_1-ring spectrum), K^inv(R) is the homotopy fibre of the cyclotomic trace K(R) → TC(R) from connective algebraic K-theory; 𝕂^inv(R) is the fibre of 𝕂(R) → TC(R) from nonconnective K-theory. Relative versions are K^inv(R, I) = fib(K^inv(R) → K^inv(R/I)).
items.locator: Definition 1.1, p. 2; Variant in §5.2, p. 41; §4.5, p. 35

items.name: Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy theorem
items.statement: If R → R′ is a surjection of rings with nilpotent kernel (more generally a map of connective E_1-rings with π_0R → π_0R′ surjective with nilpotent kernel), then K^inv(R) → K^inv(R′) is an equivalence.
items.note: RT.3 plans the relative nilpotent comparison theorem.

items.name: Henselian pairs and henselian local rings
items.statement: A pair (S, I) is henselian if I ⊆ Jac(S) and every simple root modulo I of a monic polynomial over S lifts to a root in S; a local ring is henselian if (S, 𝔪) is. Pairs complete along I are henselian.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean at 082e2d3: HenselianRing R I is exactly condition (2) of Definition 3.12 (jac and monic lifting); HenselianLocalRing.TFAE gives the local equivalences. The other two characterizations are item 043.

items.name: Gabber rigidity
items.statement: Let (R, I) be a henselian pair and n invertible in R. Then K(R)/n → K(R/I)/n is an equivalence of spectra.
items.note: L.2 plans rigidity with coefficients prime to the residue characteristic 'for the required henselian pairs'; the paper uses only the second half of Gabber's proof (henselizations of smooth algebras over fields at rational points, also in Gillet–Thomason), Remark 4.37.

items.name: Theorem A: rigidity of K^inv for henselian pairs
items.statement: Let (R, I) be a henselian pair. For every prime p the map K^inv(R) → K^inv(R/I) is an equivalence modulo p; equivalently K(R, I)/p → TC(R, I)/p is an equivalence. Hence K^inv(R)/n → K^inv(R/I)/n is an equivalence for every n.
items.note: RT.3 asks for 'the map-level square for ... a henselian pair in the proven range' without planning a proof, and the AMMN extraction marks this theorem planned there; this extraction assigns the theorem and its proof to the Part II, whose export RT.3 and the AMMN Part II then import.

items.name: Theorem B: asymptotic comparison of K and TC
items.statement: Let R be henselian along (p) with R/p of finite Krull dimension, and d ≥ 1 with [k(x) : k(x)^p] ≤ p^d for all x ∈ Spec(R/p). Then K(R)/p^r → TC(R)/p^r is an equivalence in degrees ≥ d for every r. (Theorem B: with d = sup_x log_p[k(x):k(x)^p], an equivalence in degrees ≥ max(d, 1).)

items.name: Theorem C: étale K-theory is TC at points of characteristic p
items.statement: If R is a strictly henselian local ring with residue field of characteristic p > 0, then K^inv(R)/p = 0, i.e. K(R) → TC(R) is a p-adic equivalence.

items.name: Theorem D: split injectivity of the cyclotomic trace
items.statement: For any local F_p-algebra R, n ≥ −1 and r ≥ 1, π_n(K(R)/p^r) → π_n(TC(R)/p^r) is split injective. More precisely there is a functor ν̃_r^{n+1} : CAlg_{F_p} → Ab commuting with filtered colimits and a natural map ν̃_r^{n+1}(R) → π_n(TC(R)/p^r) such that ν̃_r^{n+1}(R) ⊕ π_n(K(R)/p^r) ≅ π_n(TC(R)/p^r) for R local, compatibly in r; the decomposition holds for all R after Zariski sheafification.

items.name: Geisser–Levine: p-adic K-theory of regular local F_p-algebras
items.statement: If R is an ind-smooth local F_p-algebra (e.g. a regular local F_p-algebra), dlog[·] on symbols gives isomorphisms K_n(R; Z/p^r) ≅ W_rΩ^n_{R,log} for all n ≥ 0, r ≥ 1 (for r = 1, K_n(R; Z/p) ≅ Ω^n_{R,log} = ν^n(R)), and each K_n(R) is p-torsion-free. For general ind-smooth R there is a natural map π_n(K(R)/p) → ν^n(R) (Zariski sheafification on smooth varieties, [GL00, Th. 8.3]).
items.note: Nothing in the atlas plans Geisser–Levine; the Part II owns it as an imported theorem with its hypotheses (M.5 mentions only the Bloch–Gabber–Kato statement for Milnor K-theory of fields).

items.name: Theorem E: pro Geisser–Levine
items.statement: Let R be an F-finite regular local noetherian F_p-algebra and I ⊆ R an ideal; fix n, r ≥ 0. Then {K_n(R/I^s)}_s is p-torsion-free and dlog[·] on symbols gives an isomorphism of pro abelian groups {K_n(R/I^s; Z/p^r)}_s ≅ {W_rΩ^n_{R/I^s,log}}_s.
items.locator: Theorem E, p. 4; Theorem 5.26, p. 45; Corollary 5.32, p. 49
items.note: Proved in [Morrow-HW] when Spec R/I is a generalised normal crossing; the general case combines Theorem 5.31 with Geisser–Levine.

items.name: Theorem F: continuity of K-theory for F-finite complete noetherian rings
items.statement: Let R be a noetherian ring complete along an ideal I with R/pR F-finite. Then K(R) → lim_s K(R/I^s) is an equivalence modulo p.

items.name: Theorem G: TC/p is finitary on rings
items.statement: The functor Alg(Sp_{≥0}) → Sp, R ↦ TC(R)/p, commutes with sifted colimits, in particular with filtered colimits of rings.

items.name: Cyclotomic spectra and topological cyclic homology (Nikolaus–Scholze)
items.statement: A cyclotomic spectrum is X ∈ Fun(BS^1, Sp) with S^1-equivariant Frobenius maps φ_p : X → X^{tC_p} for every prime p; CycSp is the presentably symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category of these (a lax equalizer), with conservative, exact, colimit-preserving forgetful functor. TC(X) = Hom_CycSp(1, X), TC^−(X) = X^{hS^1}, TP(X) = X^{tS^1}; CycSp_{≥n} is the full subcategory with X ∈ Sp_{≥n}.

items.name: The Nikolaus–Scholze formula for bounded-below p-complete cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: For X ∈ CycSp bounded below and p-complete, X^{tC_q} = 0 for q ≠ p [NS, Lem. I.2.9], X^{tS^1} ≃ (X^{tC_p})^{h(S^1/C_p)} (Tate orbit lemma, [NS, Lem. II.4.2]), and TC(X) = fib(can − φ : TC^−(X) → TP(X)) [NS, Prop. II.1.9]; in the bounded-below case this agrees with the classical genuine-equivariant theory [NS, Thm. II.6.9].

items.name: THH of a ring as a cyclotomic spectrum
items.statement: For a ring (or structured ring spectrum) R, THH(R) ∈ CycSp [NS, §III.2]; TC(R), TC^−(R), TP(R) denote TC, TC^−, TP of THH(R). THH : Alg(Sp_{≥0}) → CycSp_{≥0} commutes with sifted colimits.
items.locator: Example 2.4, p. 8; proof of Corollary 2.15, p. 12

items.name: Classical TR, restriction, Frobenius and the isotropy sequence
items.statement: For p-complete X ∈ CycSp, TR^r(X; p) = X^{C_{p^{r−1}}} with maps R, F : TR^{r+1} → TR^r and V : TR^r → TR^{r+1}; TR(X; p) = lim_R TR^r, TC(X) = fib(id − F : TR(X; p) → TR(X; p)) (equation (2)), TC^r(X; p) = fib(R − F : TR^r → TR^{r−1}), and there are cofibre sequences X_{hC_{p^r}} → TR^{r+1}(X; p) → TR^r(X; p) (equation (3), [Hes96, Th. 1.2]).

items.name: Connectivity of TC
items.statement: If X ∈ CycSp_{≥n} is p-complete, then TC(X) ∈ Sp_{≥n−1}.
items.note: Two proofs: via TR and the isotropy sequence, and (Remark 2.14) purely from the Nikolaus–Scholze formula using the Adams tower for HZ^triv and Proposition 2.12.

items.name: TC/p commutes with geometric realizations
items.statement: The functor TC/p : CycSp_{≥0} → Sp commutes with geometric realizations.

items.name: TC/p commutes with all colimits on connective cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: The functor TC/p : CycSp_{≥0} → Sp commutes with all colimits (equivalently, with filtered colimits).

items.name: Inverse limits of towers of connective cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: For a tower … → X_2 → X_1 in CycSp_{≥0}, lim X_i exists in CycSp (in CycSp_{≥−1}) and is preserved by the forgetful functor; hence TC(lim X_i) ≃ lim TC(X_i).

items.name: Trivial cyclotomic spectra
items.statement: The unique symmetric monoidal cocontinuous functor Sp → CycSp, X ↦ X^triv, is left adjoint to TC; X^triv has trivial S^1-action and Frobenius X → X^{hC_p} → X^{tC_p}; S^triv is the unit.

items.name: The cyclotomic spectrum HF_p^triv
items.statement: π_*(HF_p^{tC_p}) is E(u_{−1}) ⊗ F_p[t^{±1}], |t| = −2, for p > 2 and F_2[t^{±1}], |t| = −1, for p = 2; TC^−_*(HF_p^triv) = F_p[x] and TP_*(HF_p^triv) = F_p[x^{±1}] with |x| = −2 and can the localization at x; φ_{HF_p} is an isomorphism on π_0.

items.name: The Frobenius of HF_p^triv kills x
items.statement: The Frobenius φ : TC^−_*(HF_p^triv) → TP_*(HF_p^triv) annihilates x.

items.name: Three cofibre sequences for circle actions on HZ-modules
items.statement: For X ∈ Mod_HZ(Sp^{BS^1}) there are functorial cofibre sequences Σ^{−2}X^{hS^1} →^x X^{hS^1} → X, X → X_{hS^1} → Σ^2X_{hS^1}, and Σ^{−2}X^{hS^1} →^{x·can} X^{tS^1} → X_{hS^1}, x ∈ π_{−2}(HZ^{hS^1}) the generator.

items.name: TC of HF_p^triv-modules
items.statement: For X ∈ Mod_{HF_p^triv}(CycSp) there is a functorial fibre sequence TC(X) → X → X_{hS^1}.

items.name: The unit of HF_p^triv-modules is compact
items.statement: X ↦ TC(X) on Mod_{HF_p^triv}(CycSp) commutes with all colimits; that is, the unit of this presentably symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category is compact.

items.name: Earlier special cases of the finiteness of TC/p
items.statement: Corollary 2.15 was previously accessible for commutative F_p-algebras (Hesselholt's de Rham–Witt description, §2.4), for square-zero extensions (McCarthy's p-limit axiom), and for spherical monoid rings Σ^∞_+M, whose THH has a Frobenius lift so that TC(X) fits in a fibre square with ΣX_{hS^1} and two copies of X [NS, Prop. IV.3.4, Lem. IV.3.1].

items.name: Approximating TC/p by homotopy orbits
items.statement: For each n there is a functor F : CycSp_{≥0} → Sp in the thick subcategory generated by X ↦ (X ⊗ HF_p^triv)_{hS^1} with τ_{≤n}F(X) ≃ τ_{≤n}(TC(X)/p); one may take F(X) = TC(X ⊗ τ_{≤n+1}(S^0/p)^triv).

items.name: Pro-zero towers of functors
items.statement: Let 𝒞 admit countable coproducts and {F_r} a tower of functors 𝒞 → Ab with lim_r F_r(X) = lim^1_r F_r(X) = 0 for all X and each F_r commuting with countable coproducts; then {F_r} is pro-zero in Pro(Fun(𝒞, Ab)). The same holds for towers of functors 𝒞 → Sp with lim_r F_r(X) = 0, F_r commuting with countable coproducts, and homotopy uniformly in a fixed interval [a, b].
items.note: Uses Emmanouil's criterion (Topology 35, Cor. 6): vanishing lim^1 of countable sums of a tower implies Mittag-Leffler.

items.name: The TC^r tower is pro-constant mod p
items.statement: For each k, the tower {τ_{≤k}(TC^r(−; p)/p)}_r in Fun(CycSp_{≥0}, Sp) is pro-constant with value τ_{≤k}(TC(−)/p).

items.name: The inverse Cartier operator and the Cartier isomorphism
items.statement: For an F_p-algebra R, C^{−1} : Ω^n_R → H^n(Ω^*_R) ⊂ Ω^n_R/dΩ^{n−1}_R is the multiplicative operator with C^{−1}(a) = a^p and C^{−1}(db) = b^{p−1}db; for R ind-smooth it is an isomorphism Ω^n_R ≅ H^n(Ω^*_R) (Cartier isomorphism, [Kat70, Th. 7.2]).

items.name: The de Rham–Witt complex
items.statement: For an F_p-algebra R, the de Rham–Witt complexes W_rΩ^*_R (Bloch–Deligne–Illusie) with R, F : W_rΩ^n → W_{r−1}Ω^n and V, and WΩ^*_R = lim_R W_rΩ^*_R; F reduces to C^{−1} : Ω^* → Ω^*/dΩ^{*−1}.

items.name: Hesselholt's HKR theorem for TR
items.statement: For R smooth over F_p and s ≥ 1, TR^s_*(R; p) ≅ W_sΩ^*_R ⊗_{Z/p^s} Z/p^s[σ_s], |σ_s| = 2, with R(σ_s) = pσ_{s−1} (up to a unit) and R on W_sΩ; hence TR_*(R; p) ≅ WΩ^*_R with F matching F. The comparison is induced by the map of p-typical Witt complexes λ_{s,R} : W_sΩ^*_R → TR^s_*(R; p) ([Hes96, Prop. 1.5.8]), and extends to ind-smooth algebras.
items.locator: Theorem 2.25 and equations (10)–(11), p. 15; proof of Theorem 5.31, p. 48
items.note: CR.4 assigns the THH/TR realization of de Rham–Witt to RefinedTraceMethods; no RT stage names it.

items.name: Structure of the de Rham–Witt complex of ind-smooth algebras
items.statement: For R ind-smooth over F_p: each WΩ^n_R is p-torsion-free (R kills p-torsion in W_sΩ^n, [Ill79, I.3.6]); ker(WΩ^n_R → Ω^n_R) is generated by the images of V and dV ([Ill79, I.3.18]); im(F) = {w : dw ∈ pWΩ^{n+1}} ([Ill79, I.3.21.1.5]); W_sΩ^•/p ≃ Ω^• ([Ill79, I.3.15]); and ker(d) = im(F : W_2Ω^n → Ω^n) ([Ill79, I.3.21]).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.26 and footnote 5, pp. 16–17
items.note: CR.4 plans the classical de Rham–Witt complex over perfect fields; the paper spells out the passage to ind-smooth algebras.

items.name: TC/p of F_p-algebras via de Rham–Witt
items.statement: R ↦ TC(R)/p commutes with filtered colimits of F_p-algebras. For R ind-smooth, 0 → coker(F − 1 on WΩ^{n+1}_R/p) → π_n(TC(R)/p) → ker(F − 1 on WΩ^n_R/p) → 0, and the square with rows F − 1 : WΩ^n_R/p → WΩ^n_R/p and C^{−1} − 1 : Ω^n_R → Ω^n_R/dΩ^{n−1}_R (diagram (12)) is cartesian and cocartesian.

items.name: Saturated and strict Dieudonné complexes
items.statement: A saturated Dieudonné complex is a p-torsion-free complex with F such that dF = pFd, F injective and im F = {x : p | dx}; it is strict if complete for the filtration by im(V^n, dV^n). WΩ^*_A of ind-smooth A is strict, and A ↦ WΩ^*_A commutes with filtered colimits into strict Dieudonné complexes.
items.note: CR.4 plans the BLM construction via strict saturated Dieudonné complexes.

items.name: Frobenius fixed points of strict Dieudonné complexes are finitary
items.statement: The functors (X^*, d, F) ↦ ker(F − 1 : X^*/p → X^*/p) and coker(F − 1 : X^*/p → X^*/p) from strict Dieudonné complexes to graded abelian groups commute with filtered colimits.
items.note: Stated with the remark that it 'can be proved in an entirely analogous manner' to Proposition 2.26; no separate proof is given.

items.name: Nonunital algebras
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, a nonunital R-algebra is an R-module I with a commutative associative multiplication I ⊗_R I → I; the category Ring^nu_R has all limits and colimits and is equivalent to augmented R-algebras via I ↦ R ⋉ I. R[x_1,…,x_n]^+ is free on n generators; a short exact sequence I′ → I ↠ Ī is one of underlying abelian groups.

items.name: Local nonunital algebras and localization
items.statement: I ∈ Ring^nu_R is local if every x ∈ I has y ∈ I with x + y + xy = 0 (equivalently I lies in the Jacobson radical of any R-algebra containing it as an ideal, or of R ⋉ I). Ring^{nu,loc}_R is closed under limits and sifted colimits and is reflective, with left adjoint I ↦ I[(1 + I)^{−1}] = I ⊗_{R[1+I]} R[(1+I)^{gp}]; R[x_1,…,x_n]^+_{(x_1,…,x_n)} is the free local object.

items.name: Henselian nonunital algebras
items.statement: I ∈ Ring^nu_R is henselian if for every n ≥ 1 and g ∈ I[x] the equation x(1 + x)^{n−1} + g(x) = 0 has a solution in I. Henselian implies local, the solution is unique, Ring^{nu,h}_R is closed under limits, sifted colimits and quotients, and the condition does not depend on R.

items.name: Henselization of nonunital algebras
items.statement: Ring^{nu,h}_R is presentable and the inclusion into Ring^nu_R has a left adjoint (henselization): it is the orthogonal subcategory for the maps f_{n,t} : R[x_0,…,x_t]^+ → R[x_0,…,x_t,y]^+/(y(1+y)^{n−1} + x_0 + x_1y + … + x_ty^t). R{x_1,…,x_n}^+, the henselization of R[x_1,…,x_n]^+, is the free henselian nonunital algebra on n generators.

items.name: Lawvere theories for nonunital rings
items.statement: A category 𝒞 with all limits and colimits and a conservative sifted-colimit-preserving U : 𝒞 → Sets with left adjoint F is monadic over Sets; a full subcategory closed under limits and sifted colimits whose inclusion is a right adjoint again has these properties, with free objects obtained by reflecting. Ring^nu_R, Ring^{nu,loc}_R and Ring^{nu,h}_R are of this kind; their compact projective objects are retracts of free objects.
items.note: Printed with F called the 'right adjoint' of U (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Equivalent characterizations of henselian pairs and first properties
items.statement: For a pair (S, I), equivalent: (1) simple roots mod I of every f ∈ S[x] lift; (2) I ⊆ Jac(S) and (1) for monic f; (3) S → S/I has the right lifting property against étale maps ([Stacks, Tag 09XD]). Lifts in (3) are unique; subideals of henselian ideals are henselian; locally nilpotent ideals are henselian.

items.name: Elkik's theorem
items.statement: If (S, I) is a henselian pair, S → S/I has the right lifting property with respect to smooth maps.

items.name: Gabber: henselianity depends only on the ideal
items.statement: A pair (S, I) is henselian if and only if I is henselian as a nonunital ring [Gab92, Prop. 1]; equivalently if and only if (Z ⋉ I, I) is henselian.

items.name: Henselization of pairs
items.statement: Every pair (S, I) has a henselization (S^h, I^h): the initial henselian pair under (S, I), with S^h a filtered colimit of étale S-algebras, I^h = IS^h = I ⊗_S S^h and S/I ≅ S^h/I^h ([Stacks, Tag 0EM7]); any factorization S → S̃ → S/I with S̃ ind-étale over S and S̃ → S/I henselian is the henselization.

items.name: Henselization preserves Milnor squares
items.statement: Milnor squares are cartesian and cocartesian squares of rings with surjective vertical maps (so the kernels are identified). If S → T, S′ → T′ is a Milnor square with kernels I, J, the henselizations along I and J form a Milnor square with S′, T′, and T^h ≅ S^h ⊗_S T.

items.name: Henselization of an ideal is independent of the base
items.statement: For a pair (S, I) with henselization (S^h, I^h) and any ring R → S, I^h is the henselization of I in Ring^nu_R; hence the nonunital henselization does not depend on R.

items.name: Free henselian nonunital Q-algebras
items.statement: The filtered colimit, over N ordered by divisibility, of the endomorphisms [N] : x_i ↦ Nx_i of Z{x_1,…,x_n}^+ is Q{x_1,…,x_n}^+ ([Gab92, Prop. 3]).

items.name: Finitely generated, perfect and pseudocoherent functors
items.statement: For a small category 𝒞, F : 𝒞 → Ab is finitely generated if it is a quotient of ⊕_{i≤t} Z[Hom(X_i, −)]; F : 𝒞 → Sp is perfect if in the thick subcategory generated by Σ^∞_+Hom(C, −) (the compact objects of Fun(𝒞, Sp)), and pseudocoherent if for each n some perfect F′ → F is an equivalence on τ_{≤n}. Relative versions (𝒟-perfect, 𝒟-pseudocoherent, 𝒟-finitely generated) use only corepresentables of objects of a small full subcategory 𝒟 ⊂ 𝒞.

items.name: Characterizations of pseudocoherent functors
items.statement: For F : 𝒞 → Sp_{≥d}, equivalent: F is pseudocoherent; τ_{≤n}F is compact in Fun(𝒞, Sp_{≤n}) for every n; F = colim G_i with G_{d−1} = 0 and G_i/G_{i−1} a finite sum of Σ^iΣ^∞_+Hom(C, −). F is 𝒟-pseudocoherent iff it is left Kan extended from 𝒟 and F|_𝒟 is pseudocoherent, iff it has such a filtration with C ∈ 𝒟.

items.name: Left Kan extension along a full subcategory
items.statement: For 𝒟 ⊂ 𝒞 full, Lan : Fun(𝒟, Sp) → Fun(𝒞, Sp), Lan(G)(C) = colim_{D→C, D∈𝒟} G(D), left adjoint to restriction; functors left Kan extended from 𝒟 are equivalent to Fun(𝒟, Sp).

items.name: Closure properties of pseudocoherent functors
items.statement: 𝒟-pseudocoherent functors form a thick subcategory; are closed under colimits over simplicial sets with finite skeleta and under geometric realizations of uniformly bounded below diagrams; π_d of a d-connective 𝒟-pseudocoherent functor is 𝒟-finitely generated; and if 𝒞 has finite coproducts and 𝒟 is closed under them, they are closed under smash products.

items.name: The Goodwillie tower of Σ^∞Ω^∞
items.statement: There is a natural tower {P_n(Σ^∞Ω^∞)} under Σ^∞Ω^∞ with P_1(X) ≃ X and fib(P_n → P_{n−1}) ≃ (X^{⊗n})_{hΣ_n}; for X ∈ Sp_{≥1}, Σ^∞Ω^∞X ≃ lim_n P_n(X) and the connectivity of Σ^∞Ω^∞X → P_n(X) tends to ∞.

items.name: Pseudocoherence through Σ^∞Ω^∞ and through HZ
items.statement: If 𝒞 has finite coproducts, 𝒟 is closed under them and F : 𝒞 → Sp_{≥1}, then F is 𝒟-pseudocoherent iff Σ^∞Ω^∞F is, iff Σ^∞_+Ω^∞F is. If F is 𝒟-pseudocoherent so is HZ ⊗ F; conversely if F is uniformly bounded below and HZ ⊗ F is 𝒟-pseudocoherent, so is F.

items.name: Projectively pseudocoherent functors on henselian nonunital rings
items.statement: A functor Ring^{nu,h}_R → Ab (resp. Sp) is projectively finitely generated (resp. projectively pseudocoherent) if it is 𝒟-finitely generated (resp. 𝒟-pseudocoherent) for 𝒟 = (Ring^{nu,h}_R)_Σ, the idempotent completion of the free objects R{x_1,…,x_n}^+. I ↦ Σ^∞_+I^n is projectively pseudocoherent, and projectively pseudocoherent functors commute with filtered colimits.

items.name: A Gabber-type vanishing lemma
items.statement: Let F_0 : Ring^{nu,h}_Z → Ab be projectively finitely generated, vanishing on I killed by some N > 0 and on nonunital Q-algebras, right exact on short exact sequences (F_0(I′) → F_0(I) → F_0(Ī) → 0 exact), and commuting with filtered colimits. Then F_0 = 0.

items.name: The axiomatic rigidity argument
items.statement: Let F : Ring^{nu,h}_Z → Sp be projectively pseudocoherent with (1) F(R{x_1,…,x_n}^+) = 0 for every prime field R and n; (2) F sends short exact sequences to fibre sequences; (3) F(I) = 0 for nilpotent I. Then F = 0.

items.name: Left Kan extension via simplicial resolutions
items.statement: For 𝓔 with sifted colimits and F : Ring^{nu,h}_R → 𝓔, F is left Kan extended from (Ring^{nu,h}_R)_Σ iff F commutes with filtered colimits and |F(I_•)| ≃ F(I_{−1}) for every simplicial resolution I_• of I_{−1} (free resolutions suffice); resolutions come from Quillen's model structure on simplicial objects.

items.name: Homological stability for GL_n
items.statement: H_*(BGL_n(A); Z) → H_*(BGL_{n+1}(A); Z) is an isomorphism in a range growing linearly in n whose offset depends only on the Krull dimension of the maximal spectrum of A (the stable rank) (van der Kallen [vdK80]); for Z ⋉ I with I henselian the range is that of Z.

items.name: Finiteness of classifying spaces of congruence subgroups
items.statement: GL_n(Z) has a normal subgroup N of finite index with BN homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex (Borel–Serre).
items.note: ALS.2 plans the Borel–Serre compactification.

items.name: Pseudocoherence of group homology of GL
items.statement: I ↦ C_*(BGL_∞(Z ⋉ I); Z) is projectively pseudocoherent on Ring^{nu,h}_Z (via GL_n(1 + I) ≅ I^{n^2} as sets, the bar construction and C_*(BGL_n(Z ⋉ I)) ≃ C_*(BGL_n(1 + I))_{hGL_n(Z)}).

items.name: K_0 is rigid for henselian pairs
items.statement: For a henselian pair (R, I), isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective R-modules and R/I-modules agree; K_0(R) ≅ K_0(R/I).

items.name: K-theory of rings via the plus construction
items.statement: Connective K(A) has Ω^∞K(A) ≃ K_0(A) × BGL(A)^+, so HZ ⊗ Σ^∞_+Ω^∞τ_{≥1}K(A) ≃ C_*(BGL_∞(A); Z); K_1(A) = GL(A)^ab.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.21, p. 31; proof of Proposition 4.34, p. 35

items.name: Pseudocoherence of K-theory
items.statement: I ↦ K(Z ⋉ I) is projectively pseudocoherent on Ring^{nu,h}_Z; in particular it commutes with simplicial resolutions (and this holds on nonunital local rings too).

items.name: Pseudocoherence of Eilenberg–MacLane functors
items.statement: A ↦ HA on abelian groups is Latt-pseudocoherent (Latt the finitely generated free groups), via HA = colim_n Σ^{−n}Σ^∞K(A, n) and the iterated bar construction; hence I ↦ HI is projectively pseudocoherent on Ring^{nu,h}_Z (a spectral form of Deligne's functorial free resolutions).

items.name: Pseudocoherence of THH and TC/p
items.statement: I ↦ THH(Z ⋉ I) and I ↦ TC(Z ⋉ I)/p are projectively pseudocoherent on Ring^{nu,h}_Z.

items.name: Logarithmic forms ν^n and their cokernel ν̃^n
items.statement: For an F_p-algebra R, ν^n(R) = Ω^n_{R,log} = ker(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^n_R → Ω^n_R/dΩ^{n−1}_R) and ν̃^n(R) = coker(1 − C^{−1}). ν^n is an étale sheaf generated étale-locally by dlog x_1 ∧ … ∧ dlog x_n (x_i units), ν^0 = F_p, and ν̃^n vanishes étale-locally.
items.note: [Ill79, Thm. 2.4.2] in the smooth case and [Morrow-HW, Cor. 4.2] in general.

items.name: Differential forms under étale maps in characteristic p
items.statement: For R → S étale of F_p-algebras, Ω^n_R ⊗_R S ≅ Ω^n_S, and Ω^n_R/dΩ^{n−1}_R ⊗_{R^{(1)}} S^{(1)} ≅ Ω^n_S/dΩ^{n−1}_S (the relative Frobenius square is cocartesian, [Stacks, Tag 0EBS]).

items.name: Geisser–Hesselholt: TC/p of ind-smooth F_p-algebras
items.statement: For R ind-smooth over F_p there is a functorial exact sequence 0 → ν̃^{n+1}(R) → π_n(TC(R)/p) → ν^n(R) → 0, and π_n(K(R)/p) → π_n(TC(R)/p) → ν^n(R) is the Geisser–Levine map. On smooth schemes the étale homotopy sheaves of TC/p and K/p agree via the trace and TC/p has an étale descent spectral sequence ([GH99, Th. 4.2.6]); the trace is dlog[·] on symbols ([GH99, Lem. 4.2.3, Cor. 6.4.1]).
items.locator: Theorem 4.29(2), p. 33; proof of Corollary 5.32, p. 49

items.name: K^inv of ind-smooth local F_p-algebras
items.statement: If R is an ind-smooth local F_p-algebra, π_n(K^inv(R)/p) ≅ ν̃^{n+2}(R) functorially.

items.name: Rigidity of ν and ν̃
items.statement: For a henselian pair (R, I) of F_p-algebras, ν^n(R) → ν^n(R/I) is surjective and ν̃^n(R) → ν̃^n(R/I) is an isomorphism for each n.
items.note: Key step: for s ∈ I, x − sx^n = 1 has a solution in R (Lemma 4.30), so (1 − C^{−1})(uω) = ω for a form ω vanishing mod I.

items.name: Rigidity for ind-smooth henselian local F_p-algebras
items.statement: If (R, 𝔪) is an ind-smooth henselian local F_p-algebra with residue field k, then K^inv(R) → K^inv(k) is an equivalence modulo p.

items.name: Excision for K^inv (Cortiñas; Geisser–Hesselholt; Dundas–Kittang; Land–Tamme)
items.statement: If R → S is a map of unital associative rings carrying a two-sided ideal I isomorphically onto a two-sided ideal J of S, then 𝕂^inv(R, I) → 𝕂^inv(S, J) is an equivalence (rationally Cortiñas, with finite coefficients Geisser–Hesselholt, in general Land–Tamme).
items.note: RT.3 lists excision among the named inputs of the relative comparison; this statement is the general form it should own.

items.name: K^inv of nonunital rings
items.statement: For a nonunital ring I set 𝕂^inv(I) = 𝕂^inv(Z ⋉ I, I); then 𝕂^inv(I) ≃ 𝕂^inv(R, I) whenever I is a two-sided ideal of R, and 𝕂^inv sends short exact sequences of nonunital rings to fibre sequences.

items.name: Bass excision in low degrees
items.statement: For a Milnor square, 𝕂_n(R, I) → 𝕂_n(S, J) is an isomorphism for n ≤ 0 and surjective for n = 1 ([Bass, Thm. XII.8.3]); connective and nonconnective K-theory agree in degrees ≥ 0.
items.note: K.6 plans Bass's negative K-groups and K.5 excision under the hypotheses of the adopted theorem.

items.name: Connective versus nonconnective relative K-theory for henselian pairs
items.statement: If (R, I) is henselian and R → S carries I isomorphically onto an ideal J of S, the square with rows K(R, I) → K(S, J) and 𝕂(R, I) → 𝕂(S, J) is cartesian; hence K^inv(R, I) → K^inv(S, J) is an equivalence.

items.name: The integral statement fails
items.statement: Theorem 4.36 is false integrally: for R the perfection of F_p[[x]] and I = ∪(x^{1/p^n}), K_1(R, 𝔪) = ker(R^× → F_p^×) is a nonzero Z[1/p]-module, while TC_1(R, 𝔪) is derived p-complete.

items.name: The continuity question
items.statement: For a ring R and ideal I (with R I-adically complete, or (R, I) henselian), how close is K(R) → lim_s K(R/I^s) to an equivalence? Known mod-p cases: Suslin and Panin for complete DVRs, Gabber rigidity for p invertible, Dundas in low degrees, Geisser–Hesselholt for A[[x_1,…,x_n]] with A F-finite regular local and for p-torsion-free rings of finite stable rank henselian along p, and Morrow for F-finite regular local rings complete along a generalised normal crossing ideal.

items.name: F-finite rings and their first properties
items.statement: An F_p-algebra R is F-finite if its absolute Frobenius is finite. An F-finite noetherian F_p-algebra has finite Krull dimension ([Kun76, Prop. 1.1]); a generation bound p^d over the Frobenius passes to localizations, so every residue field k has [k : k^p] ≤ p^d; henselizations of finite type F_p-algebras along ideals are F-finite and excellent ([Stacks, Tag 07QS]); for excellent R the completion R → R̂ is regular ([EGA IV_2, 7.8.3(v)]).
items.locator: Definition 5.1, p. 38; Example 6.7, p. 53; proof of Lemma 5.29, p. 46

items.name: Cotangent complexes and p-bases of F-finite rings and fields
items.statement: For R F-finite noetherian, each π_nL_{R/F_p} is a finitely generated R-module ([DM17, Cor. 3.8]); e.g. Ω^1_{F_p[[t]]/F_p} is free of rank one. For a field k of characteristic p, a family is part of a p-basis iff its differentials are linearly independent in Ω^1_k, so dim Ω^1_k = log_p[k : k^p] and Ω^n_k = 0 for n > log_p[k : k^p] ([Mat86, §26, Thm. 26.5]).
items.locator: §5.1, p. 38; proof of Theorem 5.7, p. 39; proof of Theorem 6.5, p. 53

items.name: THH mod p only sees R ⊗^L F_p
items.statement: If R → R′ induces R ⊗^L_Z F_p ≃ R′ ⊗^L_Z F_p, then THH(R) → THH(R′) is a mod p equivalence; in particular THH(R) → THH(R̂_p) is one for R noetherian.

items.name: Continuity of THH for F-finite complete noetherian rings
items.statement: If R is noetherian, complete along I ⊆ R and R/pR is F-finite, then THH(R) → lim_s THH(R/I^s) is an equivalence modulo p (extending [DM17, Thm. 4.5] from Z_(p)-algebras).

items.name: Continuity is equivalent to henselian rigidity
items.statement: Theorem 5.5 implies Theorem 4.36: reduce to henselizations of finite type Z-algebras, use Néron–Popescu and Elkik to write R → R̂ as a filtered colimit of split injections (Artin approximation), then continuity and Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy for (R̂, IR̂).

items.name: Néron–Popescu desingularization
items.statement: A regular homomorphism of noetherian rings (e.g. R → R̂ for R excellent) is a filtered colimit of smooth ring maps ([Stacks, Tag 07BW]).
items.locator: Remark 5.6, p. 39; proofs of Lemma 5.29 and Theorem 5.31, pp. 46–48
items.note: The same statement is routed to SF.0 by the Česnavičius extraction (PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-22/popescu).

items.name: Discontinuity of K-theory without F-finiteness
items.statement: If k is a field of characteristic p that is not F-finite, K(k[[t]])/p → lim_s K(k[t]/(t^s))/p is not an equivalence; it is not surjective on π_2.
items.note: The proof detects symbols by dlog into lim_s Ω^2 and bounds the weights of t-adic coefficients of forms from Ω^2_{k[[t]]}; its displayed congruences carry index slips (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Weights of 2-forms and the Bloch–Esnault–Kerz bound
items.statement: If u_1,…,u_n,v_1,…,v_n are linearly independent in a vector space V, then Σu_i ∧ v_i has weight exactly n (Lemma 5.8, via the interior product V^∨ → V of rank ≤ 2·weight). The image of Ω^2_{k[[t]]} in lim_s Ω^2_k ⊗ k[t]/(t^s) consists of Σ τ_j t^j with w(τ_j) ≤ N·C(j+2, j) for some N ([BEK14, Lem. B2], valid for any field k).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.7 and Lemma 5.8, pp. 39–41

items.name: K_2 of local rings with many units
items.statement: For local rings with infinite residue field (e.g. k[[t]], k[t]/(t^s) with k infinite), K_2^M ≅ K_2 ([vdK77, §8]).

items.name: p-adic continuity of K-theory
items.statement: K-theory is p-adically continuous for R if K(R) → lim_i K(R/p^iR) is an equivalence modulo p.

items.name: Geisser–Hesselholt p-adic continuity
items.statement: If R is a p-torsion-free local ring henselian along (p), K-theory is p-adically continuous at R, and K(R)/p → {K(R/p^iR)/p}_i is a pro-isomorphism on each π_j.

items.name: Nilpotent and quickly converging towers
items.statement: A tower {A_i} of abelian groups is nilpotent if all A_{i+N} → A_i vanish for some N, and quickly converging if some r makes {im(A_{i+r} → A_i)} eventually constant; these form an abelian subcategory closed under extensions ([Mat15, Lem. 3.10]). A tower of spectra is nilpotent if some A_{i+N} → A_i are nullhomotopic, quickly converging if cofib({lim X_i} → {X_i}) is nilpotent, almost nilpotent/almost quickly converging if every τ_{≤n} truncation is.

items.name: Formal properties of quickly converging towers
items.statement: Quickly converging towers of spectra have quickly converging homotopy towers (conversely when homotopy lies in a fixed range); almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers form thick subcategories; geometric realizations of simplicial almost quickly converging towers of connective spectra are almost quickly converging with the expected limit; and tensor products of almost quickly converging towers of connective spectra are almost quickly converging with limit X ⊗ Y.

items.name: TC/p of almost quickly converging towers
items.statement: If {X_i} is a tower in CycSp_{≥0} whose underlying tower {X_i/p} is almost quickly converging, then {TC(X_i)/p} is almost quickly converging.

items.name: Continuity of TC along towers of ring spectra
items.statement: If {R_i} is a tower of connective E_1-rings and R → lim R_i is an equivalence mod p with {R_i/p} almost quickly converging, then TC(R) → lim TC(R_i) is an equivalence mod p and {TC(R_i)/p} is almost quickly converging.

items.name: Derived p-adic continuity of TC
items.statement: For R a connective E_1-algebra in Mod_HZ, TC(R) → lim_i TC(R ⊗_HZ HZ/p^i) is a p-adic equivalence and the tower is almost quickly converging modulo p.

items.name: Derived p-adic continuity of K-theory
items.statement: If R is a connective E_1-algebra in Mod_HZ with π_0R commutative and henselian along (p), then {K(R ⊗_HZ HZ/p^i)/p} is almost quickly converging and K(R) → lim_i K(R ⊗_HZ HZ/p^i) is an equivalence modulo p.

items.name: p-adic continuity of K-theory for rings henselian along p
items.statement: If R is a commutative ring henselian along (p) with bounded p-power torsion, then K-theory is p-adically continuous at R and {K(R/p^iR)/p} is almost quickly converging.
items.note: Generalizes Theorem 5.10 (no locality, no p-torsion-freeness). Remark 5.23 notes sphere-level variants using towers of E_∞-algebras approximating S^0 p-adically.

items.name: Logarithmic de Rham–Witt groups
items.statement: For an F_p-algebra R, dlog[·] : (R^×)^{⊗n} → W_rΩ^n_R, α_1 ⊗ … ⊗ α_n ↦ dlog[α_1] ∧ … ∧ dlog[α_n]; W_rΩ^n_{R,log} is the subgroup of forms that are Zariski-locally sums of dlog forms (equivalently étale-locally). The sheaves W_rΩ^n_X on an F_p-scheme have no higher cohomology on affines, W_r of an étale map is étale and W_rΩ^n_R ⊗_{W_r(R)} W_r(S) ≅ W_rΩ^n_S for R → S étale.
items.note: CR.4 plans W_rΩ, dlog and étale descent; HL.2 introduces logarithmic de Rham–Witt coefficients. The Zariski–étale comparison is [Morrow-HW, Cor. 4.1(iii)], item 099.

items.name: Morrow's structure results for logarithmic Hodge–Witt groups
items.statement: For any F_p-algebra R: pro short exact sequences {W_rΩ^n_log}_r → {W_rΩ^n}_r →^{R−F} {W_{r−1}Ω^n}_r of étale sheaves ([Morrow-HW, Cor. 4.1(ii),(iii)]); ker(π − F̄ : W_rΩ^m_R → W_rΩ^m_R/dV^{r−1}Ω^m_R) = W_rΩ^m_{R,log} ([Morrow-HW, Cor. 4.2(iii)]); R − F is surjective on relative forms for F-finite noetherian I-adically complete R ([Morrow-HW, Prop. 2.20]); and the pro Illusie sequence for formal completions ([Morrow-HW, Cor. 4.8]).

items.name: Relative mod p K-theory of smooth henselian pairs
items.statement: If (R, I) is a henselian pair of F_p-algebras with R and R/I ind-smooth, then K_n(R, I; Z/p) ≅ Ω^n_{(R,I),log} := ker(Ω^n_{R,log} → Ω^n_{R/I,log}).

items.name: Surjectivity of R − F on relative de Rham–Witt groups
items.statement: Let R be an F_p-algebra henselian along I, with W_rΩ^n_{(R,I)} := ker(W_rΩ^n_R → W_rΩ^n_{R/I}) and W_rΩ^n_{(R,I),log} := ker(W_rΩ^n_{R,log} → W_rΩ^n_{R/I,log}). Then R − F : W_rΩ^n_{(R,I)} → W_{r−1}Ω^n_{(R,I)} is surjective.

items.name: Illusie's exact sequence for logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves
items.statement: For X smooth over a perfect field of characteristic p (and, by Shiho, for regular F_p-schemes), W_sΩ^n_{X,log}/p^r ≅ W_rΩ^n_{X,log} for s ≥ r, so 0 → {W_sΩ^n_{X,log}}_s →^{p^r} {W_sΩ^n_{X,log}}_s →^{R^{s−r}} W_rΩ^n_{X,log} → 0 is exact as pro étale sheaves ([Ill79, §I.5.7], [Shi07, Cor. 2.13]).

items.name: The relative pro Illusie sequence
items.statement: Let R be F-finite, regular, noetherian and henselian along I, and n ≥ 0. Then 0 → {W_sΩ^n_{(R,I^s),log}}_s →^{p^r} {W_sΩ^n_{(R,I^s),log}}_s →^{R^{s−r}} {W_rΩ^n_{(R,I^s),log}}_s → 0 is exact for every r ≥ 1.
items.note: The proof's displays print R^{r−s} for R^{s−r} (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Pro HKR for TR of regular F-finite rings and their quotients
items.statement: For R regular noetherian F-finite and I ⊆ R, λ_R : {W_sΩ^n_R}_s → {TR^s_n(R; p)}_s and λ : {W_sΩ^n_{R/I^s}}_s → {TR^s_n(R/I^s; p)}_s are pro-isomorphisms (Hesselholt; Dundas–Morrow [DM17, Cor. 4.15]); hence {W_sΩ^n_{(R,I^s)}}_s ≅ {TR^s_n(R, I^s; p)}_s.

items.name: Relative pro Geisser–Levine for henselian ideals
items.statement: Let R be an F-finite regular noetherian F_p-algebra henselian along I ⊆ R; fix n, r ≥ 0. The trace induces an isomorphism of pro abelian groups {K_n(R, I^s; Z/p^r)}_s ≅ {W_rΩ^n_{(R,I^s),log}}_s.

items.name: Pro comparison with Milnor K-theory and p-torsion-freeness
items.statement: For R F-finite regular noetherian and I ⊆ R with R/I local, and n, r ≥ 0: {K^M_n(R/I^s)/p^r}_s → {K_n(R/I^s; Z/p^r)}_s is surjective with the same kernel as dlog[·] : {K^M_n(R/I^s)/p^r}_s → {W_rΩ^n_{R/I^s}}_s (for classical or Kerz's improved Milnor K-theory), and {K_n(R/I^s)}_s is p-torsion-free.

items.name: Lifting classes and relative pro Geisser–Levine for local rings
items.statement: For R F-finite regular noetherian local and I ⊆ R, and n, r ≥ 0: 0 → {K_n(R, I^s; Z/p^r)}_s → K_n(R; Z/p^r) → {K_n(R/I^s; Z/p^r)}_s → 0 is short exact; there is s such that any class of K_n(R/I; Z/p^r) lifting to K_n(R/I^s; Z/p^r) is symbolic and lifts to K_n(R); and {K_n(R, I^s; Z/p^r)}_s ≅ {W_rΩ^n_{(R,I^s),log}}_s via the trace.

items.name: Rigid invariants agree on separably closed fields (after Suslin)
items.statement: Let F : Ring → Ab commute with filtered colimits and be rigid for henselian pairs. Then F(K) ≅ F(L) for any extension K → L of separably closed fields.
items.note: Suslin's argument: for a connected smooth affine k-scheme X, x^*α ∈ F(k) is independent of the k-point x. The proof prints x^*α = 0 for x_0^*α = 0 (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Étale sheaves of K/p and TC/p
items.statement: Let π_n(𝒦/p), π_n(𝒯𝒞/p) be the étale sheafifications of π_n(K(−)/p), π_n(TC(−)/p) on a scheme X and i : (X ×_Z F_p)_et → X_et. Theorem 6.1 (with TC/p = 0 where p is invertible) is equivalent to π_n(𝒯𝒞/p) ≃ i_*i^*π_n(𝒦/p), adjoint to the trace; likewise mod p^s.

items.name: p-adic étale K-theory of schemes proper over a ring henselian along p
items.statement: Let X be proper over Spec R with R henselian along (p), and K̂^ét the étale Postnikov sheafification of K. Then K̂^ét(X)/p → TC(X)/p is an equivalence.
items.note: Uses that TC/p is an étale Postnikov sheaf ([CM21, Thm. 5.16]; [GH99, §3] for affines), proper base change and Gabber's affine analogue, and Lemma 6.4.

items.name: Étale Postnikov sheafification and hyperdescent inputs
items.statement: TC/p is an étale Postnikov sheaf on qcqs schemes ([CM21, Thm. 5.16]); the Nisnevich topos of Spec R with R of finite Krull dimension has finite homotopy dimension ([CM21, Th. 3.17]; [SAG, Thm. 3.7.7.1] for R noetherian), so Postnikov towers converge; and TC/p^r is a Nisnevich sheaf (Blumberg–Mandell).
items.note: Clausen–Mathew, Hyperdescent and étale K-theory, is queued as PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21.

items.name: Proper base change
items.statement: For X proper over Spec R and torsion étale sheaves, higher direct images commute with base change.
items.note: As in the Bhatt–Mathew arc-topology extraction (item 5 there).

items.name: Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change
items.statement: If (R, I) is a henselian pair, H^j_et(Spec R, 𝓕) ≅ H^j_et(Spec R/I, 𝓕|) for torsion étale sheaves 𝓕; combined with proper base change this gives H^j_et(X, 𝓕) ≅ H^j_et(X ×_R R/pR, i^*𝓕) for X proper over R henselian along (p).
items.note: Routed with the same statement of the Bhatt–Mathew arc-topology extraction (PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21/25).

items.name: Mod p étale cohomological dimension of F_p-algebras
items.statement: For any F_p-algebra R, the mod p étale cohomological dimension of Spec R is ≤ 1.
items.note: Noetherian case by Artin–Schreier ([SGA4, X.5.1]); general case by [SGA4, IX.5.5] and commutation with filtered colimits.

items.name: Nisnevich descent for nonconnective K-theory
items.statement: 𝕂(−)/p^r is a Nisnevich sheaf of spectra on Spec R (Thomason–Trobaugh).

items.name: p-adic Lichtenbaum–Quillen for rings henselian along p
items.statement: If R is henselian along (p), Spec(R/p) has finite Krull dimension and [k(x) : k(x)^p] ≤ p^d (d ≥ 1) for all x, then K(R)/p^r → K̂^ét(R)/p^r is an equivalence in degrees ≥ d for every r.

items.name: F-finite noetherian F_p-algebras
items.statement: If R is a noetherian F-finite F_p-algebra generated by p^d elements over its Frobenius, then K(R)/p → TC(R)/p is an equivalence in degrees ≥ d (d = 0: R is a finite product of perfect fields).

items.name: K and TC of perfect F_p-algebras
items.statement: For R a perfect F_p-algebra, K(R)/p^r → TC(R)/p^r is an equivalence on connective covers: TC_i(R) = 0 for i > 0, with THH_*(R) = R[σ], TC^−_*(R) = W(R)[x, σ]/(xσ − p), TP_*(R) = W(R)[x^{±1}]; for connected Spec R, π_0(TC(R)/p^r) = Z/p^r and π_{−1}(TC(R)/p^r) = coker(F − 1 on W_r(R)); K_i(R) is a Z[1/p]-module for i > 0 because ψ^p is the Frobenius ([Hil81], [Kra80]).

items.name: Semiperfect reductions
items.statement: If R is henselian along (p) and R/p is semiperfect, then K(R)/p^r → TC(R)/p^r is an equivalence in degrees ≥ 0 for every r.

items.name: K-theory and TC of O_C
items.statement: For C a complete nonarchimedean field with perfect residue field of characteristic p (e.g. perfectoid, or C_p), (O_C, 𝔪_C) is henselian and K(O_C)/p^r → TC(O_C)/p^r exhibits the source as the connective cover of the target, recovering Nizioł's and Hesselholt's calculations for O_{C_p}.
items.note: The printed 'K(O_C; Z_p) ≃ K(C; C_p)' should read K(C; Z_p) (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Identification of the complementary summand
items.statement: For any F_p-algebra R, ν̃^m_r(R) := H^1(Spec(R′)_et; π_m(𝒯𝒞/p^r)) (R′ → R the henselized free ind-smooth cover) is naturally coker(π − F̄ : W_rΩ^m_R → W_rΩ^m_R/dV^{r−1}Ω^m_R); for r = 1 it is ν̃^m(R). The cokernel of π − F̄ is rigid for henselian pairs and π − F̄ is surjective étale-locally.
items.note: The paragraph before Theorem 6.11 defines π_{n+1}(𝒯𝒞/p^r) as the sheafification of π_n(TC(−)/p^r) (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Strictly henselian local rings and strict henselization
items.statement: A local ring is strictly henselian if it is henselian with separably closed residue field; strict henselizations exist.
items.note: Tau Ceti's Modular Curves layer 4D owns strict henselisation as general scheme-level API.

routes.title: The arc-topology and descent for étale cohomology
routes.brief: This route adds one consumer to the new roadmap proposed by the Bhatt–Mathew arc-topology extraction (PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21), which already routes Gabber–Huber's affine analogue of proper base change there (item 25). Clausen–Mathew–Morrow use it, with proper base change (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2), to reduce the torsion étale cohomology of a scheme proper over a ring henselian along (p) to its special fibre (proof of Theorem 6.3). Follow that brief. Unit tests: Spec of a henselian DVR, and a finite étale cover of it.
routes.reason: Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change is already routed to this proposed roadmap by the Bhatt–Mathew extraction.

The equivalent characterizations of henselian pairs, henselization of pairs, Elkik's theorem and Néron–Popescu are standard Stacks-project commutative algebra; SF.0 already receives Néron–Popescu from the Česnavičius extraction, and these belong with it.

R03.3 states excellence and catenarity hypotheses for local rings; Kunz's finiteness of F-finite rings, F-finiteness of henselizations and regularity of completions of excellent rings belong there, as in the Bhatt–Mathew syntomic extraction.
DD.0 owns cotangent complexes and Kähler differentials; finite generation of π_nL for F-finite rings and dim Ω^1_k = log_p[k:k^p] via p-bases are statements about them.
CR.4 owns classical de Rham–Witt theory of smooth (and, by Popescu, regular) F_p-algebras; Illusie's I.5.7 sequence for logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves and Shiho's extension are part of that theory.

CR.4 assigns the THH/TR realization of de Rham–Witt to RefinedTraceMethods, and RT.2 plans agreement with the classical TR/TC formulation; Hesselholt's HKR theorem for TR of smooth F_p-algebras is that realization.
RT.3 lists excision among the named inputs of the relative K/TC comparison; the Cortiñas–Geisser–Hesselholt–Land–Tamme excision theorem for 𝕂^inv is that input in its general form.
